title: Chronic Pain — Pacing, Graded Activity and Breaking the Boom-Bust Cycle

hook.en: Some people with long-lasting pain do too much on good days and then spend days in bed. Others stop moving because they fear harm. Both paths make pain and disability worse. Learn how pacing and graded activity help people do more, steadily, even when pain is still present.
hook.ur: Lambe arse ke dard wale kuch log achhe dinon mein bohat zyada kar lete hain aur phir din bistar mein guzarte hain. Kuch nuqsan ke dar se harkat chhor dete hain. Dono raaste dard aur ma'zoori ko barhate hain. Seekhein pacing aur graded activity kaise logon ko dard hote hue bhi musalsal zyada karne mein madad dete hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll recognise the boom-bust and avoidance patterns, set baselines for activities, build them gradually by time or amount rather than by pain, plan flare-ups, and link activity goals to what matters to the patient.
goal.ur: End tak aap boom-bust aur bachne ke patterns pehchanenge, activities ki baseline tay karenge, unhein dard ke bajaye waqt ya miqdar se aahista barhayenge, flare-ups ka plan banayenge, aur activity goals ko mareez ke liye ahem cheezon se jorenge.

text.en: In **chronic pain** (lasting more than 3 months), pain is a poor guide to tissue damage because the nervous system has become more **sensitive**. Two unhelpful patterns are common: **boom-bust** (overdoing it on good days, then crashing) and **avoidance** (doing less and less for fear of harm). **Pacing** means doing activities in **planned, manageable amounts** — set by time or quantity, not by how pain feels on the day — and **graded activity** means increasing those amounts **slowly and steadily** towards meaningful goals. The aim is to **do more and live more**, not to remove all pain first.
text.ur: **Chronic pain** (3 mahine se zyada) mein dard tissue ke nuqsan ki kamzor nishani hai kyunke nervous system zyada **hassas** ho chuka hota hai. Do ghair-mufeed patterns aam hain: **boom-bust** (achhe dinon mein zyada kar lena, phir gir jana) aur **bachna** (nuqsan ke dar se kam se kam karna). **Pacing** ka matlab activities ko **plan shuda, qabil-e-intezam miqdar** mein karna hai — waqt ya miqdar se tay, din ke dard ke ehsaas se nahi — aur **graded activity** ka matlab in miqdaron ko ma'ni-khez goals ki taraf **aahista aur musalsal** barhana hai. Maqsad **zyada karna aur zyada jeena** hai, pehle saara dard khatam karna nahi.

text.en: Boom-bust is like **driving on an empty tank, then waiting for a tow truck**. Pacing is **filling the tank regularly and driving a steady distance every day** — you cover more ground in a month, and you are never stranded.
text.ur: Boom-bust **khaali tanki par gaari chala kar phir tow truck ka intezar karne** jaisa hai. Pacing **baqaida tanki bharna aur roz ek jitna fasla chalana** hai — mahine mein zyada fasla tay hota hai, aur aap kabhi raste mein phanste nahi.

title.en: Setting up pacing and graded activity
title.ur: Pacing aur graded activity set karna

steps.title: Choose meaningful goals
steps.detail: Ask what the person wants to get back to, such as walking to the market, playing with grandchildren or working a full day. Break each goal into activities that can be measured. || Ma'ni-khez goals chunein

steps.title: Find the baseline
steps.detail: For each activity, find an amount the person can do on a good day and a bad day without a big flare (for example walking 8 minutes). Set the starting point at about 70 to 80 percent of that amount. || Baseline dhoondein

steps.title: Build up gradually by plan
steps.detail: Increase by a small, fixed amount (for example 10 percent or one more minute) every few days or each week, whether pain is high or low that day. Break tasks into chunks with short rests and change position often. || Plan ke mutabiq aahista barhayein

steps.title: Plan for flare-ups
steps.detail: Agree in advance what to do in a flare: reduce the amount for a few days rather than stopping, use comfort strategies (heat, relaxation, gentle movement), and return to the plan as it settles. || Flare-ups ka plan

question.en: A patient walks for an hour on a good day, then stays in bed for two days. What pattern is this?
question.ur: Mareez achhe din ek ghanta chalta hai, phir do din bistar mein rehta hai. Yeh kaun sa pattern hai?

feedback.en: Graded activity increases steadily without crashes.
feedback.ur: Graded activity baghair girawat ke musalsal barhti hai.

feedback.en: Yes — overactivity followed by a crash; pacing smooths it out.
feedback.ur: Haan — zyada activity ke baad girawat; pacing isay hamwaar karta hai.

feedback.en: Pacing would keep the amount similar every day.
feedback.ur: Pacing har din miqdar ek jaisi rakhti.

title.ur: Dard par munhasir ya waqt par munhasir?

rows.en: Stop when the planned amount is done
rows.ur: Plan shuda miqdar poori hone par ruko
Thora kam kiya hua plan karna

rows.en: Steady increase in what the person can do
rows.ur: Shakhs ke kaam mein musalsal izafa

text.en: **Plan, not pain, sets the pace.** Decide the amount in advance, keep it on good and bad days, and increase it slowly.
text.ur: **Plan, dard nahi, raftaar tay karta hai.** Miqdar pehle se tay karein, achhe aur bure dono din qaim rakhein, aur aahista barhayein.

text.en: **Increasing activity only when pain allows.** Waiting for pain to fall before doing more keeps people stuck, because chronic pain fluctuates for many reasons unrelated to harm. Increases should follow the plan, with flare-up plans for the hard days.
text.ur: **Sirf tab activity barhana jab dard ijazat de.** Zyada karne se pehle dard girne ka intezar logon ko phansa deta hai, kyunke chronic pain bohat si aisi wajah se ghatta barhta hai jo nuqsan se mutalliq nahi. Izafa plan ke mutabiq ho, mushkil dinon ke liye flare-up plan ke saath.

question.en: A patient's baseline is walking 10 minutes without a big flare. Where should graded walking start?
question.ur: Mareez ki baseline 10 minute chalna hai bare flare ke baghair. Graded walking kahan se shuru ho?

text.en: About 7 to 8 minutes, increased by a small fixed amount every few days
text.ur: Takreeban 7 se 8 minute, har chand din thori tay shuda miqdar barhate hue

feedback.en: Yes — start below baseline so progress is reliable.
feedback.ur: Haan — baseline se neeche shuru karein taake behtari qabil-e-aitbaar ho.

text.ur: Tezi se behtari ke liye 20 minute

feedback.ur: Yeh girawat ko daawat deta hai.

text.en: Only on days when pain is under 3 out of 10
text.ur: Sirf un dinon jab dard 10 mein se 3 se kam ho

feedback.en: That is pain-contingent and leads to boom-bust.
feedback.ur: Yeh dard par munhasir hai aur boom-bust ki taraf le jata hai.

question.en: What should happen in a flare-up?

text.en: Stop all activity until the pain is gone
text.ur: Dard khatam hone tak sab activity band karein

feedback.en: Complete rest worsens deconditioning and fear.
feedback.ur: Mukammal aaram kamzori aur dar ko barhata hai.

text.en: Reduce the planned amount for a few days and use comfort strategies, then build back to the plan
text.ur: Chand din plan shuda miqdar kam karein aur aaram ke tareeqe istemal karein, phir plan par wapas barhein

feedback.ur: Haan — kam karein, band na karein.
Yeh girawat ko gehra karta hai.

text.en: **Use the person's own diary.** A simple weekly chart of minutes walked, sitting tolerance or chores done shows progress that pain scores hide. Celebrate the gains in activity even when pain is unchanged. Combine pacing with pain education, sleep advice and, where needed, psychological support.
text.ur: **Shakhs ki apni diary istemal karein.** Chalne ke minute, baithne ki bardasht ya ghar ke kaam ka saada hafta war chart woh behtari dikhata hai jo dard ke score chhupa lete hain. Activity mein faide ka jashn manayein chahe dard waisa hi ho. Pacing ko dard ki taleem, neend ke mashware aur zaroorat ho to nafsiyati madad ke saath jorein.

question.en: Does graded activity mean the pain does not matter?
question.ur: Kya graded activity ka matlab hai ke dard ahem nahi?

answer.en: No. The pain is real, and it is taken seriously. Graded activity accepts that pain may continue for a while and focuses on rebuilding the person's life alongside it, while other treatments target the pain. Many people find that as activity and confidence grow, pain also becomes less intense or less bothersome.
answer.ur: Nahi. Dard asal hai, aur isay sanjeedgi se liya jata hai. Graded activity maanti hai ke dard kuch arsa jaari reh sakta hai aur us ke saath shakhs ki zindagi dobara banane par tawajjo deti hai, jabke doosre ilaj dard ko nishana banate hain. Bohat se log dekhte hain ke jaise activity aur aitmaad barhta hai, dard bhi kam shadeed ya kam pareshan kun ho jata hai.

beats.patient: A 45-year-old woman has had widespread back and leg pain for 2 years after a lifting injury, with normal investigations and no red flags. On good days she cleans the whole house, then rests in bed for 2 to 3 days. She wants to go to her daughter's wedding and stay for the evening.
beats.assessment: The pattern is boom-bust in chronic pain with central sensitisation features; there are no signs of serious disease.
beats.treatment: Explain pain science, set a goal (standing and sitting through a 3-hour event), find baselines for standing, sitting and walking, start at 70 to 80 percent and add a little each week, break chores into chunks and plan for flare-ups.
beats.reassess: Over 10 weeks she does a little housework daily without crashes, sits for 90 minutes and attends the wedding for the evening with planned breaks.

text.en: **Reassess for serious causes** if pain changes character, becomes constant and severe at night, or comes with weight loss, fever, new neurological symptoms or bladder or bowel changes. **Screen for low mood and risk** (hopelessness, thoughts of self-harm) and refer for support when present. Pacing and graded activity are used after serious disease has been ruled out.
text.ur: **Sangeen wajah ka dobara jaiza lein** agar dard ka andaaz badle, raat ko musalsal aur shadeed ho, ya wazan girne, bukhar, nayi neurological alamaat ya peshab ya pakhane ki tabdeeli ke saath ho. **Udasi aur khatre ki screening karein** (na-ummeedi, khud ko nuqsan ke khayalat) aur maujood hone par madad ke liye refer karein. Pacing aur graded activity sangeen bimari ke khatam hone ke baad istemal hote hain.

summary.en: In chronic pain the nervous system is more sensitive, so pain is a poor guide to harm; boom-bust and avoidance both worsen disability.
summary.ur: Chronic pain mein nervous system zyada hassas hota hai, is liye dard nuqsan ki kamzor nishani hai; boom-bust aur bachna dono ma'zoori barhate hain.

summary.en: Pacing sets activity by time or quantity (start at 70 to 80 percent of baseline), and graded activity increases it slowly by plan, not by pain.
summary.ur: Pacing activity ko waqt ya miqdar se tay karti hai (baseline ke 70 se 80 percent se shuru), aur graded activity isay plan se aahista barhati hai, dard se nahi.

summary.en: Plan flare-ups (reduce, do not stop), link goals to what matters to the person, and keep screening for red flags and low mood.
summary.ur: Flare-ups ka plan banayein (kam karein, band na karein), goals ko shakhs ke liye ahem cheezon se jorein, aur red flags aur udasi ki screening jaari rakhein.

back.en: Overdoing activity on good days, then crashing with pain and rest.
back.ur: Achhe dinon mein zyada activity, phir dard aur aaram ke saath girawat.

front.ur: Graded activity kahan se shuru hoti hai?

back.en: About 70 to 80 percent of the person's baseline.
back.ur: Shakhs ki baseline ka takreeban 70 se 80 percent.

front.ur: Waqt par munhasir vs dard par munhasir?

back.en: Stop when the planned amount is done, not when it hurts.
back.ur: Plan shuda miqdar poori hone par rukein, dard hone par nahi.

front.en: What to do in a flare-up?

back.en: Reduce the planned amount for a few days, use comfort strategies, then build back up.
back.ur: Chand din plan shuda miqdar kam karein, aaram ke tareeqe istemal karein, phir dobara barhayein.
